references.text: Joseph's brothers plan to kill him because he is their father's favorite and they are jealous, which mirrors the motivation of the vineyard workers to kill the heir in Mark 12:7.

Psalm 2:1-2 speaks of the nations' rebellion and the conspiracy of the earth's kings against the Lord and his anointed, which can be seen as a foreshadowing of the vineyard workers' conspiracy against the heir.
Isaiah 5:1-7 uses the image of a vineyard that God planted and expected justice from, but found only bloodshed and cries, paralleling the actions of the vineyard workers in Mark 12:7.
In Matthew 21:38-39, a parallel account, the vineyard workers plan to kill the son to take his inheritance, directly related to the event in Mark 12:7.
Luke 20:14-15 gives a parallel account where the vineyard workers decide to kill the heir, which reflects the event in Mark 12:7.
